Dossier note: specimen was colchicine, annotated as Microtubule destabilizers; both Scientist call and NSC vote (2/4 wells, high-similarity hits) were correct.

Phenotype fit: replicated 3 uM wells showed tubulin loss with high act/tub ratio, irregular fragmented nuclei (solidity z ~ -36), low cell count, and microscopist-confirmed loss of filamentous network — classic destabilizer arrest/cytotoxicity. Low-dose wells were weak/low-similarity and split, as expected below onset.

Literature: colchicine-site binders described as microtubule-destabilizing agents PMID:35939994, PMID:28640209; structural work on colchicine-site destabilizer effects on microtubule organization PMID:24530796.

reflection.text:
The call was correct because the replicated high-dose phenotype was extreme and specific: 3 uM in both replicates showed nuc_solidity z ~ -36 with reduced nuc_area/form_factor and large act_tub_ratio z=+28.4 and tub_mean loss, and the atlas gave 8/10 k-neighbours as Microtubule destabilizers with per-well 1-NN similarities of 0.77 and 0.742. Visual review noting lower density and destabilizer-like morphology converged with the quantitative tubulin loss.

What misled was the dose threshold: the 0.3 uM well with weak frac_mitotic_like z=+2.2 classified as Actin disruptors at similarity 0.194 and the 1.0 uM well with nuc_area z=+3.0 and tub_mean z=-2.7 classified as Kinase inhibitors at similarity 0.2, giving only a 2/4 NSC majority. I kept Eg5 inhibitors alive too long based on the microscopist suggestion and mitotic-like signal, when low-similarity intermediate-dose atlas calls should have been down-weighted.

Acquisition of the second 3 uM replicate was the decisive choice because it confirmed the saturated high-dose signal and secured the protocol vote, whereas sampling additional intermediate doses would have added more low-confidence split votes.

Correct: the call was **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (2/4). The Scientist's own call was **Microtubule destabilizers** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The call was correct because the replicated high-dose phenotype was extreme and specific: 3 uM in both replicates showed nuc_solidity z ~ -36 with reduced nuc_area/form_factor and large act_tub_ratio z=+28.4 and tub_mean loss, and the atlas gave 8/10 k-neighbours as Microtubule destabilizers with per-well 1-NN similarities of 0.77 and 0.742. Visual review noting lower density and destabilizer-like morphology converged with the quantitative tubulin loss.

What misled was the dose threshold: the 0.3 uM well with weak frac_mitotic_like z=+2.2 classified as Actin disruptors at similarity 0.194 and the 1.0 uM well with nuc_area z=+3.0 and tub_mean z=-2.7 classified as Kinase inhibitors at similarity 0.2, giving only a 2/4 NSC majority. I kept Eg5 inhibitors alive too long based on the microscopist suggestion and mitotic-like signal, when low-similarity intermediate-dose atlas calls should have been down-weighted.

Acquisition of the second 3 uM replicate was the decisive choice because it confirmed the saturated high-dose signal and secured the protocol vote, whereas sampling additional intermediate doses would have added more low-confidence split votes.

What was right:
- Prioritized high-dose 3 uM wells where nuc_solidity z=-36.0/-36.8, act_tub_ratio z=+28.4 and tubulin loss gave strong destabilizer signal in e3 and e8
- Used describe_phenotype e4 and compare_to_reference_atlas e5/e9 together, with 8/10 k-neighbours as Microtubule destabilizers supporting the final 0.88 hypothesis
- Acquired a 3 uM replicate e8 to confirm the severe nuclear irregularity and low cell counts (157 and 145 cells) rather than relying on a single well

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted weak intermediate-dose signals: 0.3 uM frac_mitotic_like z=+2.2 and 1.0 uM tub_mean z=-2.7 led to Actin disruptor and Kinase inhibitor 1-NN calls at similarities 0.194 and 0.2
- Retained Eg5 inhibitors at 0.10 then 0.05 on the basis of visual suggestion and mitotic-like features despite atlas votes favoring destabilizers
- Missed the sign flip in dose response — nuc_area z=+3.0 at 1 uM versus z=-9.2 at 3 uM and tub_glcm_contrast positive at 0.3 uM then negative at 1.0 uM — and did not explicitly resolve it before conclusion

Proposed next experiment: Tubulin washout and microtubule regrowth assay with fixed alpha-tubulin immunofluorescence and phospho-histone H3 mitotic index across 0.3, 1.0 and 3.0 uM to test for reversible tubulin loss versus persistent mitotic arrest.
